content: The Roundabout PlayPump is an innovative water pump system that harnesses the kinetic energy generated by children playing on a merry-go-round to pump water from underground sources. This system is manufactured by the South African company Roundabout Outdoor and functions similarly to a windmill-driven water pump. It is particularly effective in areas where water must be accessed from deep underground, up to 100 meters, using a borehole. The cost of installing a PlayPump is approximately R96,000 (around US$14,000), making it suitable for shared use in villages. Currently, there are over 700 PlayPumps installed across sub-Saharan Africa, providing clean drinking water to more than one million people living in poverty. On September 20, 2006, during the Clinton Global Initiative, First Lady Laura Bush announced a $16.4 million public-private partnership aimed at installing additional PlayPumps. This initiative marked the beginning of an ambitious effort to install 4,000 PlayPumps by 2010, with the goal of providing clean water to up to 10 million people in Africa. The funding for this initiative included $10 million from the U.S. government, $5 million from the Case Foundation, and $1.4 million from The MCJ Foundation. The PlayPump system operates by connecting a playground merry-go-round to a water pump. As children spin the merry-go-round, underground water is pumped into a storage tank with a capacity of 2,500 liters, which is elevated seven meters above the ground. The stored water can then be easily accessed through a tap valve. According to the manufacturer, the PlayPump can pump up to 1,400 liters of water per hour from a depth of 40 meters. Any excess water is redirected back underground. The storage tank is equipped with four advertising panels. Two of these panels are used for commercial advertisements, which generate revenue for the maintenance of the pump, while the other two panels display public health messages, such as information on HIV/AIDS prevention. Currently, there are more than 900 PlayPumps installed in four countries within sub-Saharan Africa, providing clean drinking water to approximately one million people. The PlayPump system offers numerous benefits to the communities it serves. Sub-Saharan Africa faces a severe shortage of clean water and has the highest prevalence of HIV/AIDS in the world. The PlayPump not only provides access to clean water but also delivers critical public health messages that can help prevent the spread of HIV. In 2000, the PlayPump received the World Bank’s Development Marketplace Award for its dual effectiveness in pumping water and disseminating HIV/AIDS awareness messages through the advertising panels on its water towers. Beyond the health benefits of clean and accessible drinking water, the PlayPump system has a positive impact on education and community life. By reducing the time children spend fetching water, the system allows them to attend school more regularly. Additionally, women who previously had to carry heavy containers of water over long distances can now spend more time at home or engage in activities that contribute to their families' food supply or income. Roundabout Outdoor is the company responsible for manufacturing, installing, and maintaining PlayPump systems throughout sub-Saharan Africa. PlayPumps International, a nonprofit organization, raises funds to donate these systems to African communities and schools in need. PlayPumps International is registered as a U.S. 501(c)(3) organization and as an independent South African non-governmental organization. In addition to its work in Africa, Roundabout PlayPumps have been installed in various attractions around the world to raise awareness about the transformative impact these systems have on African communities.
